title: Warren Easton school band and the Armistice Day strike
summary: He recalls teacher Mike Capera, a student strike on Armistice Day, and the school band whose members later turned professional. Louis Prima was not in it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you play in a school band too?

Well, I went to Warren Easton and Mike Capera was the music teacher out there. And at that time, he didn't like me at all. I should mention that. And when I came into a certain misfortune at one time, he read it out and practically told the class, see if you guys don't behave yourselves, you'll do the same thing. Let me deviate. This is another epic story in my life. For several years after World War I, November the 11th, almost this day, was a holiday. And this particular year, the school board and its wisdom decided it would not be a holiday. And so somebody, some nut, some kid organized a strike. And at noon, he started to march around the building, gathering cohorts, you know, until finally, practically, the whole Sioux was in line. And we marched away from the school and went downtown. We took the day off. It was a holiday. We went down to the Picayune, at that time at Lafayette Square. We had our picture taken, about 300 guys. And the next day, every one of us was sentenced to 100 days after school, one hour, plus three days suspension. And that's the one that Capera, he was tickling to death that I had been hit. But now let's go back to your school band deal. Yes, we had a school band, but all we did was play in the school auditorium. We didn't go out for the football games. We had no uniforms. I don't ever remember being in a parade. And because the only guys who would study music in those days were those who later became professionals. Practically everybody in the band, most of these are dead people today, but I'm thinking of Jake Ginsberg on a trumpet, myself on saxophone, a guy by the name of Willie Rosenblum who had turned professional and long since gone. And name after name like that, but they came out of the school band, that particular school band. Was Prima in the band at that time? No. Oh no. I thought Leon, I mean Louis went to Jesuits. He went to Warren Eason. That's what I understand. It could be very possible. Because he was not in the band when I was, I was there from 23 to 26 and I went back in 27 because I wanted to take a few more courses that I needed. I was going to apply for Tulane. You know where Tulane is of course. And I wanted some more credits and I went back for half term, or what is a full term from September to January. But Louis was not in that band. Louis would have been at least two or three years younger than I am, so it's possible that he came along later on. I didn't get to meet Louis until, when would it have been, when I was with his brother Leon's band, Leon Prima and Sharko and we were rehearsing for the old Hollywood. And then Louis used to come around then and I got to know him. Because Louis' band consisted of himself, Fazzola, Johnny Viviana, and a couple of other kids his own age.
